title: The PImpl idiom and the C++26 std:indirect type
summary: This article explores the PImpl (Pointer to Implementation) idiom in C++ and how the upcoming C++26 std::indirect type simplifies its implementation, replacing traditional approaches using raw pointers or std::unique_ptr with a more elegant and safer solution.
problem_solved: Addresses the complexity and verbosity of implementing the PImpl idiom for ABI-safe compilation and implementation hiding in C++.
why_valuable: Provides early guidance on using C++26's std::indirect to write cleaner, safer code with automatic resource management for the PImpl pattern.
